stem.en: Suppose the price of petrol doubles. Which change in demand is most likely?

text.en: The demand for electric cars rises, because they do not need petrol.
The demand for petrol cars rises, because petrol has become more valuable.
The demand for buses and trains falls, because all travel now costs more.
No other demand changes, because only the price of petrol has changed.

explanation.en: Petrol and petrol cars are complementary goods, so costlier petrol makes petrol cars less attractive. Electric cars, buses and trains can replace a petrol car, so they are substitutes, and the demand for them is likely to rise. The price of one good can change the demand for other goods.

hints.en: Which goods are used with petrol, and which can replace a petrol car?
